title: Influence of puncture angle on the visibility of arterial cannulas during ultrasound-guided puncture in phantom and cadaver models – a study among medical students
summary:
Ultrasound-guided arterial puncture is an important practical skill in medical training. Before performing the procedure on patients, it is commonly practiced using training models known as gel phantoms. However, it remains unclear how realistically these models represent actual conditions in the human body.

In this study, medical students are shown standardized ultrasound images of needles inserted at different angles in gel phantoms and cadaver models. Participants are asked to assess whether the needle tip is clearly visible and whether they would feel confident advancing the needle under these conditions.

The aim of the study is to evaluate how suitable different training models are for teaching purposes and to identify factors that influence needle visibility in ultrasound imaging. The findings may help improve training in ultrasound-guided vascular access.

interventions.name: Medical students participating in an anonymous online survey, assessing standardized ultrasound images of arterial cannulas from phantom and cadaver models with regard to needle tip visibility and perceived safety of further needle advancement.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical students
Voluntary participation in the anonymous online survey
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of voluntary participation in the anonymous online survey
